prompt:
Add and export `isExpiringSoon(item, now, days = 3)` in src/expiry.js: true when the item has not expired and expires within `days` days (use `daysLeft`). Then make `GET /expiring` use it and accept `?days=N` (default 7, so the current behavior stays). `days` must be a whole number from 0 to 365; anything else answers status 400. `handle(path, now)` receives the path with its query string.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: I added and exported `isExpiringSoon(item, now, days = 3)`, built on `isExpired` and `daysLeft`. `GET /expiring` now uses it and takes `?days=N` (default 7). Values outside whole numbers 0–365, including an empty value, get a 400 with error code `invalid_days`. `npm test` (7/7) and `npm run lint` pass, and manual calls for each case gave the expected results. Things you might not expect: `?days=0` always returns an empty list, because the existing `isExpired` already counts an item expiring today as expired. `handle` now matches routes by path alone, so `/items?x=1` returns the item list instead of a 404. The real server now passes the full URL, query string included, to `handle`. I also updated the README route entry and added a line under Unreleased in the CHANGELOG.
